summary: 1038年称帝建大夏，创西夏文、立番汉官制，三败宋军而与宋辽鼎立的西夏开国之主。
summary_en: The founding ruler of Western Xia, who proclaimed himself emperor of Great Xia in 1038, created the Tangut script and a dual Tangut–Han official system, defeated Song armies three times, and stood as a third power alongside Song and Liao.

portrait.appearance_basis: 《宋史》卷485夏国传：「性雄毅，多大略，善绘画……圆面高准，身长五尺余。少时好衣长袖绯衣，冠黑冠，佩弓矢。」定稿前依此容貌与冠服描写作艺术想象。

timeline.title: 袭夏王位
timeline.summary: 李德明卒，元昊嗣位，加速去宋化与民族国家建构。
timeline.summary_en: On Li Deming's death, Yuanhao succeeded and accelerated de-Songification and nation-building.

timeline.title: 创制西夏文
timeline.summary: 命野利仁荣等造番书（西夏文），改服饰官制，强化主体性。
timeline.summary_en: He ordered Yeli Renrong and others to devise the Tangut script, reformed dress and officialdom, and asserted Xia distinctiveness.

timeline.title: 取瓜沙肃
timeline.summary: 攻取河西走廊要地，奠称帝版图基础。
timeline.summary_en: He seized key prefectures of the Hexi Corridor, laying the territorial base for his imperial claim.

timeline.title: 河西称帝
timeline.summary: 即皇帝位，国号大夏，改元，与宋辽并立。
timeline.summary_en: He took the imperial title under the dynastic name Great Xia, changed the era, and stood alongside Song and Liao.

timeline.title: 三川口之战
timeline.summary: 宋夏大战之一，夏军获胜。
timeline.summary_en: One of the great Song–Xia battles; Xia forces won.

timeline.title: 好水川大捷
timeline.summary: 宋夏大战中夏军重创宋军，确立西夏军事地位。
timeline.summary_en: Xia forces crushed the Song army, establishing Western Xia's military standing.

timeline.title: 定川寨之战
timeline.summary: 再创宋军，确立军事优势。
timeline.summary_en: Another heavy defeat for Song forces confirmed Xia's military edge.

timeline.title: 庆历和议
timeline.summary: 宋夏达成和议，元昊对宋称臣而自帝其国，换岁赐与边境稳定。
timeline.summary_en: Song and Xia made peace; Yuanhao styled himself a subject to Song while reigning as emperor at home, trading form for annual payments and border stability.

timeline.title: 辽夏和战
timeline.summary: 与辽冲突后和，宋辽夏三角外交。
timeline.summary_en: After clashes with Liao came peace—triangular diplomacy among Song, Liao, and Xia.

timeline.title: 没藏氏与后嗣
timeline.summary: 遇弑后幼主谅祚继立，外戚没藏氏格局形成。
timeline.summary_en: After the assassination the child ruler Liangzuo succeeded, and the consort clan Mozang came to power.

timeline.title: 遇弑
timeline.summary: 元昊在宫廷斗争中被刺死，西夏转入后续诸帝。
timeline.summary_en: Yuanhao was stabbed to death amid palace struggles; Western Xia passed to its later rulers.

timeline.title: 番汉官制
timeline.summary: 设中书枢密等，番汉分号。
timeline.summary_en: He established the Secretariat, Bureau of Military Affairs, and more, with separate Tangut and Han designations.

bio_md:
# 西夏景宗 · 主要事迹

李元昊是西夏实际的开国之主。1032 年父李德明卒，他袭夏王位，随即加速去宋化与民族国家建构；1038 年在兴庆府即皇帝位，国号大夏，改元天授礼法延祚，正式与宋、辽并立。本页以《宋史·卷485·夏国传》为年表主线，《辽史》相关纪为二手入口。

称帝前后，他完成了一整套国族符号与制度建构：命野利仁荣等造番书（西夏文），改服饰官制，又设中书、枢密等机构，番汉分号。这套"强化主体性"的路线，与[[n-wei-xiaowen|北魏孝文帝]]的汉化改革恰好方向相反，对读可见中古北方政权处理自身身份的两种极端路径。

武功方面，约 1036 年他攻取瓜、沙、肃等河西走廊要地，奠定称帝版图——这条走廊正是[[han-wu-di|汉武帝]]时代开通的西北命脉，千年之后成为大夏立国的根基。1040 年三川口、1041 年好水川、1042 年定川寨，夏军连续三年重创宋军，确立了西夏的军事地位；好水川一役尤为宋夏战争的名场面（互见《宋史》任福等列传）。

连战之后是外交收尾。1044 年宋夏达成庆历和议：元昊对宋称臣而自帝其国，以名实分离换取岁赐与边境稳定；同年与辽冲突后言和，在宋、辽、夏三角之间周旋得体。文治、武功、韬略三线，至此把一个河西政权立成了鼎立之一极。

1048 年，元昊在宫廷斗争中被刺死，幼主谅祚继立，外戚没藏氏掌权——国祚并未随他个人终结，西夏转入后续诸帝。需要说明的是，宋、辽史书对西夏站位偏贬，本项目月旦取中；西夏文创制等细节仍待专书补证。

bio_parts_en.value:
Li Yuanhao was the de facto founder of Western Xia. In 1032 his father Li Deming died and he succeeded as Prince of Xia, at once accelerating de-Songification and nation-building; in 1038 he proclaimed himself emperor at Xingqing, took the dynastic name Great Xia, and changed the era to Tianshou Lifa Yanzuo, formally standing alongside Song and Liao. This page takes 《宋史·卷485·夏国传》 as the backbone of its chronology, with the relevant annals of 《辽史》 as a secondary entry point.

Around his proclamation he completed a whole set of national symbols and institutions: he ordered Yeli Renrong and others to devise the Tangut script, reformed dress and officialdom, and established organs such as the Secretariat and the Bureau of Military Affairs under separate Tangut and Han designations. This line of "asserting distinctiveness" ran in exactly the opposite direction from the sinicization of

; read together, they show the two extreme paths by which medieval northern regimes handled their own identity.

On the military side, around 1036 he seized Gua, Sha, Su, and other key points of the Hexi Corridor, laying the territorial foundation for his imperial claim—the very corridor opened in the age of

as the northwest lifeline, which a thousand years later became the ground on which Great Xia was founded. At Sanchuankou in 1040, Haoshuichuan in 1041, and Dingchuanzhai in 1042, Xia forces mauled the Song armies three years running and established Western Xia's military standing; Haoshuichuan in particular is the famous set piece of the Song–Xia war (cross-referenced in the biographies of Ren Fu and others in 《宋史》).

After the string of victories came the diplomatic wrap-up. In 1044 Song and Xia reached the Qingli settlement: Yuanhao styled himself a subject toward Song while reigning as emperor within his own realm, trading the split between name and fact for annual payments and a stable border; the same year, after clashes with Liao, he made peace, maneuvering deftly within the Song–Liao–Xia triangle. Civil construction, military success, and statecraft together had by now raised a Hexi regime into one pole of a tripartite standoff.

In 1048 Yuanhao was stabbed to death amid palace struggles; the child ruler Liangzuo succeeded, and the consort clan Mozang took power—the dynasty did not end with his person, and Western Xia passed to its later rulers. It should be noted that Song and Liao historiography is biased against Western Xia, so this project's appraisal takes a middle position; details such as the creation of the Tangut script still await confirmation from specialized scholarship.
